title: Why do big companies keep getting hacked?
description:
It’s not unusual to receive an email that your personal information has been accessed through a data breach or cyber attack these days. This happened to millions of ASOS customers in October. Or you might have logged onto a site and been told to change your password because it’s been found in a hack.

Loads of us are talking about how to protect yourself online, especially in cases where companies are responsible for handling your sensitive information.

BBC’s Cyber Correspondent Joe Tidy tells us about some of the methods cyber criminals use to carry out their hacks. We also get Tejal Reddy, a software engineer and cyber-security content creator to answer some of your online safety questions and concerns.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討大型企業頻繁遭受網路攻擊與資料外洩的原因及防範方法。節目以 ASOS 購物應用程式遭駭客侵入並推送勒索通知的事件為例，邀請 BBC 記者 Joe Tidy 分析駭客如何透過假冒員工身分進行「大獵捕」勒索。此外，網路安全專家 Tejal Reddy 針對民眾提問提供實用建議，主張使用者應實施「資料最小化」、優先使用驗證器應用程式設定 2FA 雙重驗證，並指出企業應落實「最小權限原則」以避免單點破壞影響整體系統。受訪者最後指出，雖然資料外洩令人焦慮，但一般民眾遭受嚴重損害的風險依然較低。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores why major companies continue to suffer cyberattacks and how individuals can better protect their personal data. BBC cyber correspondent Joe Tidy discusses recent high-profile breaches such as the ASOS attack, explaining how hackers use impersonation and aggressive extortion tactics to target large corporations. Cybersecurity expert Tejal Reddy also answers listener questions, recommending data minimization, advocating for authenticator apps over SMS for two-factor authentication, and stressing the importance of the principle of least privilege for corporate data security.
